result.topic_en: Euler introduces the abbreviations p^λ for the single sum ∫1/z^λ and q^μ for the double sum ∫(1/z^μ)(1/y^ν), and tabulates the resulting relations between these sums for orders m+n = 3, 4, 5 and 6.

items.quote: pro $\int\frac{1}{z^{\lambda}}$ ſcribatur $p^{\lambda}$; tum vero loco formulae $\int\frac{1}{z^{\mu}}\left(\frac{1}{y^{\nu}}\right)$ ſeu $\int\frac{1}{z^{\mu}}\left(\frac{1}{z^{\lambda-\mu}}\right)$ ſcribatur $q^{\mu}$; hincque aequationes ſingulorum ordinum magis euadent perſpicuae.
items.english: For ∫1/z^λ let p^λ be written; and in place of the formula ∫(1/z^μ)(1/y^ν), or ∫(1/z^μ)(1/z^(λ−μ)), let q^μ be written; hence the equations of the individual orders will become clearer.
